answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line runs at 94% and has no buffer, so continuity is binding. Finance still requires an 18% spend cut. Deferral (c5) was for a non-critical month-to-month case and would drop supply here. A second source (c3) does not replace the expiring primary in time and does not clearly deliver the cut. Switching primary cut unit cost and onboarded quickly once (c2), but with no buffer that still raises delivery risk the objective forbids. Incumbent renewal historically kept integration and deliveries intact (c1). Negotiation at renewal previously moved price and payment terms (c4), and longer commitments unlocked volume pricing without shrinking scope (c6). Intend to negotiate incumbent price, term, and volume on the full primary contract to pursue the mandated cut on the existing path. Uncertain whether past margin recovery or volume pricing approaches 18%; verifying c4 and c2 for magnitude and switching friction. Downstream production value is at risk if supply slips.
